newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK stocks end on hefty gains after Wall St records.
newsitem.headline: HK stocks end on hefty gains after Wall St records.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks continued their powerful advance for the fifth day in a row on Tuesday, closing on hefty gains as Monday's record highs on Wall Street swept local prices higher, brokers said.
The Hang Seng Index jumped 180.00 points, or 1.34 percent, to 13,579.34. The index hit an intra-day high of 13,679.92, the first time it has been above 13,600 points since late February.
Turnover was HK$15.40 billion, the fourth heaviest ever, compared with HK$14.92 billion on Monday.
"Sentiment in the Dow has turned around," said Peter Lai, associate director at OCBC Securities.
"And people believe that there will be no interest rate increase this month," he said.

The Dow industrials rose 143.29 points, or 2.03 percent, on Monday to an all-time closing high of 7,214.49, buoyed by mounting expectations of a capital gains tax cut in the United States and hopes that inflation remains in check.
Analysts said Hong Kong was also attracting flows from other Asian markets which were not performing as well.
"That is why the momentum in the Hong Kong market is very strong, reflected in the high turnover over the past two days," said Lai.

But Patrick Chia, research director at China Everbright Research, said he was cautious following the Hang Seng Index's 978.92 point, or 7.77 percent, advance over the last five sessions. "I think profit-taking is possible," he said.
Chia said although investors were hoping that the U.S. Federal Reserve would not raise interest rates at its May 20 meeting, there was still a possibility it could do so.
"Even if there is not an interest rate hike in the short term, the (interest rate) trend is still up so that will cap the upside," said Chia.
Lai saw "temporary resistance" at 13,700 to 13,800 points.
"After some consolidation at the lower levels of say 13,200, the market can go up again," he added.
HSBC Holdings Plc soared to another record high at HK$207.00 before closing at HK$205.00, up HK$3.00.

Property stocks lost their early momentum, with Cheung Kong (Holdings) Ltd closing down HK$0.50 at HK$73.00 after rising to a high of HK$75.25. Henderson Land Development Co Ltd slipped HK$0.50 to HK$70.00 after rising to HK$72.50 earlier.
Jewellery manufacturer and retailer Luk Fook Holdings (International) Ltd ended its first trading day at HK$1.23 compared with an initial public offering price of HK$1.00.
